AUTHORIZED LEGAL-HOLD RELEASE EVENT  - The post-hold deletion process resumes only after an explicitly authorized Legal Hold release has been formally recorded. - The release event must include an immutable UTC timestamp, the authorized releasing authority, the affected tenant, exact document/version scope, and the corresponding original deletion request ID. - An informal notification or an unverified request to release a Legal Hold must not trigger deletion. - The authority approving the Legal Hold release must be independently authorized to make that decision.  2. POST-RELEASE PURGE DEADLINE  Adopt the following rule:  - If the original 24-hour purge deadline has not yet expired when the Legal Hold is released, the original deadline remains applicable. - If the original 24-hour deadline has already expired during the authorized Legal Hold period, all affected primary-storage content must be permanently purged within a maximum of 24 hours from the recorded authorized Legal Hold release timestamp. - Deletion must resume immediately after the authorized release is recorded. - The post-release deadline must not be interpreted as permission to delay deletion unnecessarily.  3. PRESERVATION OF ORIGINAL DELETION RECORDS  The system must preserve the original deletion approval and deadline without modification.  The following timestamps and evidence must be retained separately:  - Original deletion request timestamp. - Original explicit deletion approval timestamp. - Original calculated 24-hour purge deadline. - Legal Hold authorization timestamp. - Legal Hold scope and documented legal basis. - Authorized Legal Hold release timestamp. - Identity and authority of the releasing individual. - Post-release purge deadline, where applicable. - Actual deletion execution and final verification timestamps.  The original deletion approval, original deadline, and Legal Hold history must never be overwritten or silently recalculated.  4. LEGAL-HOLD SCOPE AND AUTHORITY  - Legal Hold must apply only to the explicitly documented tenant, document, version, and content scope. - Only an explicitly authorized Legal Authority may approve or release a Legal Hold. - The Legal Hold must not create general tenant-content access or retrieval permission. - Platform Admins must not gain tenant-content access through the Legal Hold process. - A Legal Hold must not automatically authorize retention of unrelated content. - Any modification to the hold scope must be separately authorized and audited.  5. AI RETRIEVAL AND CONTENT EXCLUSION  - Content approved for deletion must remain excluded from AI retrieval and citation throughout the Legal Hold period. - Legal Hold release must not reinstate retrieval eligibility. - Following authorized release, the deletion process must resume without requiring another deletion approval. - Physical deletion must be verified before reporting the primary-storage purge as complete. - Previously deleted or deletion-approved content must never become AI eligible merely because a Legal Hold has ended.  6. FAILURE HANDLING AND ESCALATION  - If post-release deletion fails, the existing retry, monitoring, and escalation requirements remain applicable. - If the applicable post-release deadline is missed, the deletion must be marked Overdue and escalated to designated Operations / Security personnel. - The affected content must remain excluded from AI retrieval. - No unauthorized individual may bypass the original deletion authorization or Legal Hold release requirements.  7. BACKUP AND AUDIT RETENTION  - The existing maximum 30-day encrypted-backup age-out policy remains applicable. - The 365-day content-free audit-retention policy remains unchanged. - Legal Hold release must not silently reset backup or audit-retention clocks. - Any legally mandatory exception must have explicit authority, scope, justification, and audit evidence. - Backup restoration must continue to reapply all applicable deletion records before restored content becomes accessible.  8. EXPLICIT POLICY DECISION  An authorized Legal Hold may temporarily suspend physical deletion but does not reverse deletion approval or restore AI retrieval eligibility.  The original deletion approval and deadline remain immutable.  If the original deadline expires during a valid Legal Hold, physical purge must complete within 24 hours of the formally recorded authorized release.  These requirements preserve the original 24-hour purge policy while providing a controlled and auditable mechanism for legally required temporary retention.  This clarification does not authorize implementation or any bypass of existing tenant-isolation, authorization, or deletion controls., failed_rejected_retention=Intentionally replace the draft obligation; retain an explicit schedule decision gate before the affected capability proceeds, rationale_deferrals=Q5 FOLLOW-UP CLARIFICATIONS — RATIONALE, PRECISE POLICY DETAILS AND REMAINING DEFERRALS  1. OVERALL POLICY RATIONALE  The selected first-release policy prioritizes data protection, immediate AI retrieval exclusion, controlled physical deletion, tenant isolation, and independently verifiable audit evidence.  Deletion, legal retention, lifecycle retention, and AI retrieval eligibility are separate concerns and must not be treated as interchangeable permissions.  The policy deliberately establishes clear mandatory controls while keeping unresolved retention schedules and implementation details subject to explicit future decisions.  2. Q5-C01 — VALIDITY EXTENSION SAFEGUARDS  Confirm that validity extensions cannot bypass:  - Independent non-submitter approval. - Formal Knowledge Re-review. - The mandatory 180-day review policy. - Current document validity and authorization requirements. - Existing retrieval eligibility restrictions.  Changing a validity date alone must never restore AI retrieval eligibility or constitute automatic reapproval.  Any extension must follow the established independent approval and review process.  3. Q5-C02 — LEGAL RETENTION IS NOT RETRIEVAL PERMISSION  Confirm that content covered by an approved deletion request must never be reinstated for AI retrieval, including after Legal Hold release.  Legal retention exceptions apply only to otherwise eligible content that is not already covered by an approved deletion.  Any permitted use of other legally retained content must independently satisfy all Q2/Q3 approval, validity, review, tenant authorization, and retrieval eligibility requirements.  Legal Hold must not create additional Platform Admin tenant-content access or bypass existing security controls.  4. Q5-C03 — PURGE DEADLINE AFTER LEGAL-HOLD RELEASE  Adopt the following precise rule:  - Preserve the original deletion approval timestamp and original 24-hour purge deadline. - Record Legal Hold authorization, exact scope, authority, start timestamp, and release timestamp separately. - If the original purge deadline remains in the future at authorized hold release, retain that original deadline. - If the original deadline has expired during the authorized Legal Hold, complete primary-storage purge within a maximum of 24 hours from the formally recorded authorized release timestamp. - Resume deletion immediately after authorized release. - Legal Hold release must not restore AI retrieval eligibility or cancel the original deletion approval.  5. Q5-C04 — FAILED/REJECTED UPLOAD PURGE VERSUS DEFERRAL  Explicitly replace the draft requirement that automatically mandates deletion of all failed/rejected uploads and derived content within 24 hours.  The selected policy is:  - Failed and rejected content must remain excluded from AI retrieval and citation. - Rejection or processing failure alone does not automatically trigger physical deletion. - Failed and rejected content must not be retained indefinitely by default. - Their respective retention and deletion schedules must be explicitly defined and approved before the affected upload/lifecycle capability proceeds. - The schedule must separately address failed uploads, rejected uploads, original files, extracted content, chunks, embeddings, temporary files, and other derived copies. - An explicitly approved deletion request remains subject to the established 24-hour primary-storage purge obligation. - This replacement does not waive the general 24-hour deletion policy or authorize undocumented retention.  6. Q5-C05 — FIRST-RELEASE POLICY RATIONALE  The selected approach provides a practical balance between security, operational reliability, legal obligations, and storage management.  The 24-hour primary-storage purge ensures timely removal of authorized deletion targets.  The 30-day encrypted-backup age-out provides a bounded backup retention period.  The 365-day content-free audit retention preserves accountability and deletion evidence without retaining deleted business content in audit records.  Separating lifecycle retention from retrieval eligibility prevents historical, rejected, expired, superseded, or overdue knowledge from becoming AI eligible merely because it remains stored.  7. REMAINING EXPLICIT DEFERRALS  The following decisions remain unresolved and require explicit approval before the corresponding capability proceeds:  A. Lifecycle-specific retention schedules: - Failed document retention duration. - Rejected document retention duration. - Superseded version retention duration. - Expired document retention duration. - Overdue/pending-re-review content retention duration.  B. Technical implementation details: - Backup infrastructure and expiry automation. - Audit storage and evidence protection architecture. - Component-specific deletion verification. - Retry intervals, retry limits, and escalation SLAs. - Detailed monitoring and notification mechanisms. - Backup restoration validation implementation.  C. Compliance details: - Applicable jurisdiction-specific data retention obligations. - Formal Legal Hold workflow and designated legal authority. - Evidence requirements for exceptional legal retention. - Controlled release and expiry of any legally required retention exception.  These deferrals must remain visible as unresolved decisions and must not be treated as approved defaults.  8. NON-NEGOTIABLE SECURITY AND GOVERNANCE BOUNDARIES  All previously established Q2/Q3/Q4/Q5 controls remain applicable:  - Independent non-submitter approval. - Mandatory 180-day re-review. - Strict tenant isolation. - No self-approval or privilege escalation. - No exceptional Platform Admin tenant-content access in the first release. - Immediate AI retrieval exclusion for deleted or ineligible content. - No automatic reinstatement after Legal Hold release. - No reporting of unverified deletion as successful. - Backup restoration must reapply applicable deletion records. - Content-free audit evidence must remain protected.  No deferred decision creates an undocumented exception, indefinite retention permission, or implementation bypass.  9. FINAL DECISION STATUS  The Q5 deletion and retention policies and their follow-up clarifications are recorded as explicit requirement decisions.  The lifecycle-specific retention schedules and identified technical/compliance details remain deferred.  These clarifications do not constitute PRD approval, Requirement approval, implementation authorization, or permission to start another lifecycle process.  Any subsequent change must be explicitly documented, reviewed for cross-requirement consistency, and independently approved through the established governance process.
